name: UnitTypeMetadataRecord
description: Recovered 88-byte per-unit-type metadata record in the data segment. The decompiler split this record into overlapping globals (`g_UnitTypeMetadataRecords`, `g_UnitSpriteFolders`, `g_UnitTypeFlags`, and the byte_512570+ tables), but the code consistently indexes it as a single family.

fields.name: localized_name_ptrs
fields.notes: Pointer to the localized name array used by battle logs and building/unit info screens. The decompiler emitted this header as `char *(*...)[102]`, but asm/xref evidence shows at least 35 type records and one duplicated commander localized-name triplet.

fields.name: sprite_folder_name
fields.notes: Folder stem used to build paths such as `units_go\peon?.s32` and the other unit sprite-sheet filenames.

fields.name: move_pixel_speed
fields.notes: Per-frame marching displacement used by the world and battle movement animators.

fields.name: move_tick_delay
fields.notes: Delay between successive movement animation updates.

fields.name: death_frame_interval
fields.notes: Interval between death-animation frames; also reused by some idle animation loops.

fields.name: type_flags
fields.notes: Recovered flag word. Bit0 marks flying/airborne units; another bit still controls the 6-vs-10 initialization path at slot +11.

fields.name: road_move_cost
fields.notes: Road/track movement cost copied into merged stack movement profiles.

fields.name: terrain_move_costs[8]
fields.notes: Per-terrain movement-cost profile consumed through `g_TerrainMoveTableOffsets` by `Map_GetUnitTileMoveCostOrZero` and stack-level movement merging.

fields.name: move_sound_stem
fields.notes: Per-type movement sound stem used to build `sfx\ruchy\<stem>...` paths in both world and battle movement audio.

fields.name: move_sound_variant_count
fields.notes: Number of alternating movement-sound variants for footstep-style movers.

fields.name: move_sound_base_volume
fields.notes: Default playback volume passed into `CSS_PlaySound` for movement audio.

evidence: The code indexes `g_UnitTypeMetadataRecords` by `22 * unitType`, i.e. 88 bytes per type, then reads both pointer fields and late-byte movement fields from the same base address.

The decompiler's `char *(*...)[102]` type on the base pointer is misleading if read literally as the roster size: asm xrefs expose at least 35 records, while the final commander pair reuses one localized-name pointer triplet.
Battle/UI helpers dereference field 0 as a localized name pointer array, while sprite loaders read field 4 as the folder stem used in `units_go`, `units_i`, and related file paths.

Movement helpers copy bytes `+29..+37` into a merged stack profile, airborne flag checks read the overlapping flag dword at offset `+18`, and movement-audio helpers read fields `+81`, `+85`, and `+86` from the same record family.

name: UnitStackRecord
description: Per-army stack record inside gameData holding tile coordinates, ownership, slots, and the cached move path.

fields.name: tile_row
fields.notes: Row on the 200-column world grid used to stamp tile occupancy and fog-of-war.

fields.name: tile_column
fields.notes: Column on the world grid; combined with row to index TILE_INDEX.

fields.name: owner_player_index
fields.notes: Player id copied from PLAYER_DATA and reused by fog-of-war and turn-sensitive ownership checks via g_CurrentPlayerIndex.

fields.name: facing_direction
fields.notes: 0-7 direction used by sprite/orientation logic during path highlighting.

fields.name: unit_slots[10]
fields.notes: Ten embedded 31-byte slot records storing per-unit runtime state for the stack.

fields.name: path_buffer
fields.notes: Movement track copied in/out by qmemcpy during path planning.

evidence: Unit_Create uses 147174 + 725 * index to address stacks, writing row/column/facing before stamping TILE_INDEX.
UnitSlot_InitFromType writes the slot fields (type id, owner, action points, health, fatigue, morale, and control bits) at offsets relative to stackPtr + 6.
UnitStack_UpdateVision and UnitStack_HasReadyUnits read these slots and field offsets to drive fog-of-war and readiness states.

name: UnitSlotRecord
description: Recovered 31-byte per-unit runtime slot embedded inside each UnitStackRecord.

fields.name: unit_type_id
fields.notes: -1 marks an empty slot; otherwise indexes the 88-byte unit-type metadata family.

fields.name: owner_player_index
fields.notes: Copied from the stack owner when the slot is initialized.

fields.name: current_action_points
fields.notes: Seeded from `g_UnitTypeBaseActionPoints` and recomputed from fatigue by `UnitSlot_CalcActionPointsFromFatigue` each new turn.

fields.name: current_health_percent
fields.notes: Starts at 100, scales the effective melee/ranged/damage helpers, and dropping to zero kills the slot.

fields.name: fatigue
fields.notes: 0-100 exhaustion counter. Thresholds at 80/90/100 reduce action points, and severe fatigue lowers morale each new turn.

fields.name: morale
fields.notes: Bounded 0-20 combat bonus and obedience score. Light-unit records seed this to 6, other units to 10.

fields.name: stance_bits
fields.notes: Low two bits feed melee/ranged/siege attack helpers directly; upper bits also drive garrison stance/formation cycling.

fields.name: state_flags
fields.notes: Bit 0x2 suppresses fatigue recovery for spent turns, bit 0x4 marks low-morale refusal, and bit 0x8 marks a still-ambiguous special-entry state.

fields.name: aux_runtime_state
fields.notes: Cleared on init and reused by battle/movement helper families; exact subfields remain unresolved.

fields.name: state_bits_2
fields.notes: Low bit is cleared on init and bit 0 influences ranged attack scaling in `UnitStats_CalcEffectiveRangedAttack`.

evidence: UnitSlot_InitFromType writes a stable 31-byte layout with type id, owner, current action points, health, fatigue, morale, and several control-bit clusters.
`UnitSlot_CalcActionPointsFromFatigue`, `Unit_NewTurn`, `Unit_CheckLowMorale`, and the attack helpers all reuse the same byte offsets, confirming the runtime-slot field boundaries.
The UI unit-info pane draws a damage bar from slot +9, morale badges from slot +11, and fatigue icons from slot +10, independently corroborating the field meanings.

name: MapTileRecord
description: Per-tile terrain and overlay record inside gameData used by movement, bridge placement, and terrain-edge rendering.

fields.name: terrain_tile_id
fields.notes: Primary terrain id; movement helpers index dword_52456C with this word to select the terrain-specific byte_512586 move-cost column.

fields.name: overlay_tile_id
fields.notes: Secondary visual or edge overlay inspected by draw helpers when stitching neighboring coast and terrain-edge sprites.

fields.name: road_or_bridge_tile_id
fields.notes: Non-0xFFFF marks a road, bridge, or track overlay; movement switches to byte_512585 road costs when this word is present, and bridge code temporarily writes ids such as 872 here.

evidence: Map_GetUnitTileMoveCostOrZero and UnitStack_GetTileMoveCostOrZero read word 0 through dword_52456C and test word 2 for the road-cost fast path.

Bridge movement code at clash95.c:27193-27278 writes and later restores the word at offset +4 on the crossed tile and its neighbors, proving this field belongs to the tile record rather than a transient path buffer.
Main-map rendering reads the first two words of adjacent 14-byte entries to choose seam and edge sprites.

name: TileTrapOwnerMaskLayer
description: One-byte per tile owner mask for planted traps and revealed trap knowledge.

fields.name: owner_mask
fields.notes: Bit N marks player N as the trap owner or as having revealed the trap on that tile; the byte is cleared once the trap triggers.

evidence: Trap_New writes 1 << owner into gameData + 576374 + 100 * row + column when a trap is planted.
Trap_GetTileOwnerMask returns either the raw byte or a single-player bit test, and render code draws the trap marker only when the current player's bit is present.
Trap_ClearTileOwnerMask zeroes the byte, and Trap_TriggerAtStackTile clears the same location after damaging the moving stack.

name: PlayerRuntimeState
description: Per-player runtime state block embedded in gameData. Campaign, skirmish, and mission loaders reset this block before seeding player names, controller settings, camera positions, queen state, and the deferred prisoner-placement queue.

fields.name: is_active
fields.notes: Set to 1 when a scenario loader enables this player slot; zeroed by `PlayerRuntimeState_ResetDefaults` for unused slots.

fields.name: display_name
fields.notes: Localized/player-entered ruler name copied in both campaign loaders and the multiplayer setup menu.

fields.name: camera_left
fields.notes: Saved strategic-map camera X position restored when this player becomes the viewed player.

fields.name: camera_top
fields.notes: Saved strategic-map camera Y position paired with `camera_left`.

fields.name: controller_mode
fields.notes: Multiplayer setup writes values 0, 1, or 2 here before `Scenario_LoadMultiplayerMapAndSeedPlayers`; many gameplay paths treat nonzero as locally controlled/human-visible.

fields.name: prisoner_transfer_queue[10]
fields.notes: Ten 6-byte entries cleared by `PlayerRuntimeState_ResetDefaults` and filled by `Prisoner_QueueCapturedUnit` before castles absorb new prisoners.

fields.name: queen_mood
fields.notes: Mood state read and updated by the queen-event logic.

fields.name: queen_whim
fields.notes: Current queen whim/request state used by queen review and event selection.

fields.name: queen_next_review_turn
fields.notes: Turn counter threshold checked before the queen reviews this player's kingdom again.

evidence: `PlayerRuntimeState_ResetDefaults` clears a 1423-byte region, restores the default `doc` name at offset `+4`, and initializes the first byte of each embedded 6-byte prisoner-queue entry to `-1`.

Campaign and skirmish setup code copies five 1423-byte records into `gameData + 140024`, then `Scenario_LoadMultiplayerMapAndSeedPlayers` reads enabled flags, controller settings, and player names from that region while seeding the loaded map.

`Game_AdvanceToNextPlayerTurn` and map-load helpers store and restore the per-player camera through offsets `+15` and `+19`, while queen logic uses the final bytes at `+1419..+1421` as stable per-player mood/review fields.

name: WorldViewState
description: Shared gameData region that stores world dimensions, the active scripted mission id, the current camera origin, and which player owns the active turn versus the current human view.

fields.name: map_width_tiles
fields.notes: Horizontal tile count derived at map load and used to clamp camera movement.

fields.name: map_height_tiles
fields.notes: Vertical tile count derived at map load and used to clamp camera movement.

fields.name: map_view_left
fields.notes: Current leftmost visible tile in the main-map camera.

fields.name: map_view_top
fields.notes: Current topmost visible tile in the main-map camera.

fields.name: active_mission_index
fields.notes: `-1` for free/skirmish maps; otherwise indexes the scripted mission dispatcher, mission-status text table, and mission-specific victory/failure checks.

fields.name: turn_owner_player_index
fields.notes: Player id whose strategic turn is currently active; save/load restores g_CurrentPlayerIndex from this slot.

fields.name: viewed_player_index
fields.notes: Player id whose saved camera position and visibility should drive the current UI view; usually the current human player.

evidence: Map load computes offsets 140000 and 140004 by scanning the 14-byte tile grid until it reaches sentinel 0xFFFF rows and columns.
`UI_ShowMissionStatusPanel`, the post-victory mission-advance path, and the mission jump table rooted at `Scenario_LoadMissionByIndex` all treat offset `140017` as the active mission id.
Render_RestoreLostSurfaces, keyboard scrolling, and recentering clamp offsets 140008 and 140012 against the width and height fields, proving they are the camera origin.

Game_AdvanceToNextPlayerTurn persists PLAYER_CAMERA_LEFT/TOP for g_CurrentPlayerIndex, writes TURN_OWNER_PLAYER_INDEX when the acting player changes, and restores MAP_VIEW_LEFT/TOP from PLAYER_CAMERA_LEFT/TOP(VIEWED_PLAYER_INDEX).

name: BuildingRecord
description: Per-building gameplay record inside gameData holding tile ownership, garrison slots, add-ons, and local upgrade/resource state.

fields.name: tile_row
fields.notes: Building anchor tile row used with TILE_INDEX and building footprint stamping.

fields.name: tile_column
fields.notes: Building anchor tile column used with TILE_INDEX and adjacency scans.

fields.name: owner_player_index
fields.notes: Player id copied into spawned unit stacks and used for ownership, vision, and income lookups.

fields.name: footprint_class
fields.notes: Controls which neighboring offsets are legal for exit/spawn scans and which add-on requirement table to use; exact enum values remain ambiguous.

fields.name: garrison_slots[12]
fields.notes: Stored unit entries copied into and out of temporary army stacks by Building_UnitsLeave and Building_UnitGetInto.

fields.name: garrison_order_bytes[12]
fields.notes: Per-slot packed task bytes: bits `0..2` are the train/order countdown, while bits `3..5` are the repair countdown.

fields.name: addon_type_ids[12]
fields.notes: `-1` marks an empty add-on slot; buy/remove/select helpers treat this as the installed building add-on list.

fields.name: selected_addon_slot_index
fields.notes: Tracks the currently selected production-licence slot for `Building_SetUnitProduction` and `Building_StopUnitProduction`.

fields.name: building_flags
fields.notes: Bitfield used by add-on gating, castle UI toggles, and income modifiers.

fields.name: upgrade_stage_index
fields.notes: Incremented when the timer at `+429` expires and checked against `(level_bits & 7) - 1` before starting another staged upgrade.

fields.name: upgrade_timer_turns
fields.notes: Per-turn countdown that gates completion of the staged upgrade tracked at `+421`.

fields.name: stored_resource_pool
fields.notes: Spendable local pool consumed by transfer and add-on purchase helpers and replenished by building income logic; exact economy resource label remains ambiguous.

fields.name: level_bits
fields.notes: Low three bits encode the building's current level or tier cap for upgrade/add-on checks.

fields.name: prisoner_slots[3]
fields.notes: Castle-only prisoner cells updated by `Prisoner_SetInCastles`, `Prisoner_NewTurn`, and the execution/torture/ransom helpers.

evidence: Building_Transfer, Building_UnitsLeave, and Building_UnitGetInto all index `gameData + 509674 + 467 * buildingIndex`, proving a stable per-building stride and header.
The garrison move helpers copy 31-byte unit entries between `+18` and temporary stack records, showing that `+18` begins a 12-slot building garrison array.

Building buy/remove/select helpers at clash95.c:53980-54120 operate on `+402`, `+414`, and `+416`, while upgrade and income helpers use `+421`, `+429`, `+438`, and `+444`, exposing a second stable cluster for add-ons and local economy state.

Prisoner_SetInCastles, BuildingPrisoner_SetAction, Prisoner_NewTurn, and Prisoner_Pay all operate on the 6-byte cells starting at `+445`, proving that the building record also embeds a fixed three-slot prison subarray.

name: PortRuntimeState
description: Six-dword world-session region inside gameData tracking the unique port's location and reinforcement schedule.

fields.name: port_tile_row
fields.notes: `-1` marks no port on the loaded map; otherwise this is the top-left row of the 2x2 port footprint.

fields.name: port_tile_column
fields.notes: Top-left column of the active port footprint.

fields.name: next_supply_turn
fields.notes: Absolute game-turn number when the next supply ship should arrive.

fields.name: supply_ready_flag
fields.notes: Non-zero while reinforcements are waiting to be claimed from the port.

fields.name: pending_supply_unit_count
fields.notes: Number of units to seed into the spawned reinforcement stack when the player collects the supply shipment.

fields.name: shoreline_variant_flag
fields.notes: Controls which shoreline-piece variant `Port_BuildShorePieces` renders for the current supply state.

evidence: `Port_FindAndInit` seeds all six dwords together after scanning the map for the unique port tile and then immediately calls `Port_BuildShorePieces` and `Rules_LogPortLocation`.
`Port_NewTurn`, `Port_BuildShorePieces`, and `Port_GetSupply` all read and mutate the same contiguous six-dword block to manage shipment timing, shoreline visuals, and spawned reinforcement contents.
The top-of-file offset macros in `clash95.c` and the matching xrefs in `clash95.asm` agree on the exact offsets `586374..586394` inside `gameData`.

name: QueenWhimRecord
description: Overlapped queen-whim table in the data segment. Hex-Rays split the record into `word_5191F0` and `off_5191F2`, but the queen turn logic indexes it as one 14-byte record family.

fields.name: required_frontline_score
fields.notes: Compared against `AI_CalcFrontlineScore` before the whim can be accepted, then deducted by `AI_ApplyFrontlineScore` on success.

fields.name: localized_text_ptrs[3]
fields.notes: Localized whim request text indexed by `g_LanguageIndex` in `Queen_ShowWhimDialog`.

evidence: `Queen_NewTurn` computes `7 * whimIndex`, reads a uint16 from `word_5191F0 + 7 * index`, and a localized text pointer from `off_5191F2 + 7 * index + 4 * language`, which matches one overlapped record rather than two unrelated arrays.
The same uint16 is passed into `Queen_ShowWhimDialog` and, on acceptance, into `AI_ApplyFrontlineScore`, proving it is the whim cost field rather than a pointer or enum.
`0x519350 - 0x5191F0 = 0x160`, which fits 25 records of `2 + 3*4` bytes with the expected alignment before the next table.

name: PlayerPrisonerTransferQueue
description: Per-player queue of newly captured prisoner units waiting to be assigned to a castle prison.

fields.name: prisoner_type_id
fields.notes: Type `33` or `34` copied from the captured special unit entry.

fields.name: variant_or_payload_byte
fields.notes: Auxiliary prisoner metadata copied from the captured slot; exact gameplay meaning remains unresolved.

fields.name: capture_tile_row
fields.notes: Capture-site row later used to choose the nearest eligible castle in `Prisoner_SetInCastles`.

fields.name: capture_tile_column
fields.notes: Capture-site column paired with `capture_tile_row` for nearest-castle placement.

evidence: `Prisoner_QueueCapturedUnit` appends 6-byte entries at `PLAYER_DATA(player) + 141381`, storing the captured type id plus one byte and two words copied from the special unit slot.

`Prisoner_SetInCastles` scans exactly 10 of these entries, compares the stored row/column against castle coordinates, and clears the queue entry once the prisoner is moved into a building prison slot.

name: BuildingPrisonerSlot
description: Six-byte prisoner cell embedded inside a building record.

fields.name: prisoner_type_id
fields.notes: Special prisoner unit type; `-1` marks an empty prison cell.

fields.name: variant_or_payload_byte
fields.notes: Auxiliary prisoner metadata copied from the player transfer queue; exact meaning remains ambiguous.

fields.name: turns_held
fields.notes: Incremented every prisoner turn and used to auto-trigger late actions.

fields.name: pending_action
fields.notes: 0 = none, 1 = behead, 2 = torture, 3 = pay/ransom path.

fields.name: ransom_value
fields.notes: Price/value field recalculated by `BuildingPrisoner_RecalculateRansomValue` and consumed by `Prisoner_Pay`.

evidence: `Building_FindFreePrisonerSlot` scans three 6-byte cells beginning at `building + 445` and treats byte 0 == -1 as empty.
`BuildingPrisoner_SetAction` and `BuildingPrisoner_GetAction` read and write byte `+3`, while `Prisoner_NewTurn` increments byte `+2` and `Prisoner_Pay` consumes word `+4`.
